source.title: Safe Evolution with Circuit Anchors
source.authors: Yan Liu; Jie Fu; Tsung-Yi Ho

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. There is an internal model-name inconsistency in Section 4.3: the text gives Llama-3.2-2B-Instruct for the numerical intervention result, while the figure labels Llama-3.2-1B.
record.tranche_reason: The paper intervenes on a multi-feature safety circuit and measures refusal, refining the causal-mediation claim at circuit level. It does not test the original difference-in-means direction or compare that direction with the circuit.
record.gate_note: Section 4.3 reports activation scaling of a traced safety circuit and a random-feature control on harmful prompts. These rows bear on causal mediation of refusal, but the intervention is not the claimed single difference-in-means residual-stream direction. Other reported results on evolution training, capability and over-refusal do not test the listed claim versions. The paper does not report harmless-prompt refusals after adding the circuit.
record.test_reason: The study cites Arditi et al. only in related work. Its causal experiment scales a transcoder-feature 'safety circuit' (1.2–1.8% of MLP transcoder features, chosen by attribution to refusal logits). It is not a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means residual direction, and the paper never compares the two. The circuit is then used as an anchoring tool during self-evolution. The intervention measures a related but different object, so it goes under fits_no_version, not as a test of V1 or V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that unconstrained self-evolution (EVOL-RL, Abs-ZERO) drops refusal by about 25 points. They also conclude that anchoring a small, causally verified safety circuit via a KL constraint keeps refusal above 95% with capability gains matching unconstrained evolution, beating a reward-model constraint. The circuit-intervention results serve to validate their circuit, not to test the single-direction claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses transcoder-based feature attribution to identify a multi-feature safety circuit, then scales those features' activations. It does not identify a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream mean-difference direction or project that direction out at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation scale changes refusal: suppression reduces it, while amplification yields a modest increase. Random-feature scaling has no systematic effect. The text does not give exact per-model scale results beyond the stated Llama numerical result.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling an attribution-selected transcoder safety circuit (<2% of features) to zero cuts AdvBench refusal from 96.2% to 48.7% in Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Scaling to 10x gives 99.4%. Equal-size random features show no systematic effect (±8%). The text says Qwen and Gemma follow the same pattern.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sparse set of MLP transcoder features, selected by attribution to refusal, is necessary for much (but not all) of harmful-prompt refusal in small instruct models.

record.problems: The causal intervention is on a feature circuit rather than the claim's single direction. Most per-model intervention values are reported only in Figure 3, with no exact textual values or uncertainty estimates. The text and figure disagree on whether the Llama model is 1B or 2B. No intervention experiment measures general capability or harmless-prompt refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted for the claim versions tested. The remaining evolution, capability, and over-refusal results are not rows because they do not intervene on or measure the claimed direction or its predicted behavior.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, directional ablation, activation addition on harmless prompts, or capability check under intervention.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial-training test.
A multi-feature circuit is used, but no comparison is made with single-direction, affine, or cone accounts.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
The self-evolution fine-tuning degrades refusal, but no test of whether a removable direction exists.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (tests/T5) and its V1 limits_scope label are removed: the circuit is a different construct from the claimed direction. The Llama model-name inconsistency resolves to 1B. There are internal inconsistencies: λ is 0.1 in §4.4 but 0.8 in §4.5. Also, 'Safety Score' and 'refusal rate' are used interchangeably.

versions.untested_parts: Tests suppression and amplification of a traced safety circuit against harmful-prompt refusal, not the specified harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction. Does not project the direction out of every layer and position, measure refusal on harmless prompts after addition, or evaluate general capabilities under the intervention.
No test of attacks suppressing the claimed direction or of training against its ablation.
Identifies and intervenes on a multi-feature circuit, but does not compare directional, affine, cone, or multi-direction accounts.
Does not separately test harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Studies self-evolution of already instruction-tuned models, not how or when refusal training determines whether the claimed direction exists.
No reasoning-model test of the claimed direction.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-2B-Instruct (Section 4.3 text; model name conflicts with Figure 3 label)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled safety-circuit feature activations to zero.
rows.note: The text describes the reduction as dramatic and says it demonstrates that the circuit is necessary; substantial refusal remains. The named model conflicts with the figure label Llama-3.2-1B.
rows.check: The object is a transcoder feature circuit, not the difference-in-means direction. The subject is almost certainly Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct: §4.1 lists only the 1B model, Figure 3 labels 1B, and 96.22% matches the 1B starting refusal rate in §4.4. '2B' in §4.3 looks like a typo. Zeroing leaves 48.7% refusal, so the drop is partial.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Safety-circuit suppression on harmful prompts in the reported causal-intervention experiments
reader_labels.reason: Circuit suppression lowers harmful-prompt refusal, but the explicit zeroing result leaves refusal at 48.7%; the experiment does not establish the claimed single difference-in-means direction or the other parts of V1 (r1-r4).
